sentences.zh: 3宋公剔成之弟偃襲攻剔成。

translations.literal: 3 The younger brother of Duke Ticheng of Song, Yan, launched a surprise attack on Ticheng.
translations.idiomatic: 3 Duke Ticheng of Song's brother Yan struck and overthrew him.

sentences.zh: 剔成奔齊，偃自立爲君。

translations.literal: Ticheng fled to Qi; Yan installed himself as ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Ticheng fled to Qi; Yan made himself ruler.

sentences.zh: 1秦公子華、張儀帥師圍魏蒲陽，取之。

translations.literal: 1 The Qin lords Hua and Zhang Yi led troops to besiege Puyang in Wei and took it.
translations.idiomatic: 1 Prince Hua of Qin and Zhang Yi besieged Wei's Puyang and took it.

sentences.zh: 張儀言-{於}-秦王，請以蒲陽-{復}-與魏，而使公子繇質-{於}-魏。

translations.literal: Zhang Yi said to the King of Qin, asking that Puyang be returned to Wei and that the young lord Yao be sent as hostage to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yi asked the King of Qin to return Puyang to Wei and send Prince Yao to Wei as hostage.

sentences.zh: 儀因説魏王曰：「秦之遇魏甚厚，魏不可以無禮-{於}-秦。

translations.literal: Yi then said to the King of Wei, “Qin has treated Wei with great generosity; Wei cannot be without courtesy toward Qin.
translations.idiomatic: He then told the King of Wei, “Qin has shown Wei great favor; Wei must not slight Qin.

sentences.zh: 」魏因盡入上郡十五縣以謝焉。

translations.literal: ” Wei thereupon surrendered all fifteen counties of Shang commandery by way of thanks.
translations.idiomatic: ” Wei thereupon ceded all fifteen counties of Shang commandery in gratitude.

sentences.zh: 張儀歸而相秦。

translations.literal: Zhang Yi returned and became chancellor of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yi returned and became Qin's chancellor.

sentences.zh: 1秦縣義渠，以其君爲臣。

translations.literal: 1 Qin made Yiqu a commandery and took its lord as vassal.
translations.idiomatic: 1 Qin turned Yiqu into a commandery and reduced its lord to vassal.

translations.literal: 2 Qin returned Jiao and Quwo to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: 2 Qin returned Jiao and Quwo to Wei.

sentences.zh: 1趙肅侯薨，子武靈王〔雍〕立<ref>子武靈王〔雍〕立-{據}-《史記·趙世家》索隱補。

translations.literal: 1 Marquis Su of Zhao died; his son King Wuling [Yong] succeeded<ref>King Wuling [Yong] succeeded—supplied from Shiji “House of Zhao,” Suoyin.
translations.idiomatic: 1 Marquis Su of Zhao died; his son King Wuling [Yong] succeeded<ref>King Wuling [Yong] succeeded—from Shiji “House of Zhao,” Suoyin.

sentences.zh: </ref>。

translations.idiomatic: </ref>.

sentences.zh: 置博聞師三人，左、右司過三人，先問先君貴臣肥義，加其秩。

translations.literal: He appointed three Broad-Hearing Masters and three Left and Right Fault-Finders; he first consulted his father's honored minister Fei Yi and raised his rank.
translations.idiomatic: He named three Masters of Broad Hearing and three Left and Right Fault-Finders; he consulted his father's old minister Fei Yi first and raised his rank.

sentences.zh: 1夏，四月，戊午，秦初稱王。

translations.literal: 1 In summer, the fourth month, on wuwu day, Qin first styled itself king.
translations.idiomatic: 1 In summer, fourth month, on wuwu day, Qin first took the title of king.

sentences.zh: 2衞平侯薨，子嗣君立。

translations.literal: 2 Marquis Ping of Wei died; his son Lord Si succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: 2 Marquis Ping of Wei died; his son Lord Si succeeded.

sentences.zh: 衞有胥靡亡之魏，因爲魏王之-{后}-治病。

translations.literal: In Wei (衛) there was a convict laborer named Xu Mi who fled to Wei (魏) and there treated the queen's illness.
translations.idiomatic: A convict named Xu Mi fled the state of Wei (衛) for Wei (魏) and treated the queen's illness there.

sentences.zh: 嗣君聞之，〔使人〕請以五十金買之<ref>〔使人〕請以五十金買之章校「十二行本『之』下有『使人』二字；

translations.idiomatic: Lord Si heard and [sent a man] offering fifty gold to buy him<ref>[sent a man] offering fifty gold—Zhang's collation: “In the twelve-line edition, after ‘him’ stand ‘sent a man’;

translations.idiomatic: Tui Zhai's collation agrees.

sentences.zh: 五反，魏不與，乃以左氏易之。

translations.literal: Five times he sent envoys; Wei would not yield him, so he exchanged the district of Zuoshi for him.
translations.idiomatic: Five embassies failed; Wei refused, so he traded the district of Zuoshi for the man.

sentences.zh: 左右諫曰：「夫以一都買一胥靡，可乎？

translations.literal: Those at his side remonstrated, saying, “To buy one convict laborer with an entire district—is that permissible?”
translations.idiomatic: His counselors said, “Trade a whole district for one convict—is that wise?”

sentences.zh: 」嗣君曰：「非子所知也。

translations.literal: ” Lord Si said, “This is not what you understand.
translations.idiomatic: ” Lord Si said, “You do not understand.

sentences.zh: 夫治無小，亂無大。

translations.literal: In governing there is no trifle; in disorder there is no great matter.
translations.idiomatic: In good order nothing is too small; in chaos nothing is too great.

sentences.zh: 法不立，誅不必，雖有十左氏，無益也。

translations.literal: If the law is not established and punishments are not certain, even ten Zuoshi districts would be of no use.
translations.idiomatic: If law does not stand and punishment is uncertain, ten Zuoshis would not help.

sentences.zh: 法立，誅必，失十左氏，無害也。

translations.literal: If the law is established and punishment is certain, to lose ten Zuoshi districts does no harm.
translations.idiomatic: If law stands and punishment is sure, losing ten Zuoshis does no harm.

sentences.zh: 」魏王聞之曰：「人主之欲，不-{聽}-之不祥。

translations.literal: ” When the King of Wei heard, he said, “A ruler's desire—failure to heed it is ill-omened.
translations.idiomatic: ” The King of Wei heard and said, “When a lord desires something, to refuse him is ill-omened.

sentences.zh: 」因載而往，徒獻之。

translations.literal: ” He had Xu Mi carried there and presented him as a gift without payment.
translations.idiomatic: ” He had Xu Mi carried to Wei and gave him away outright.

sentences.zh: 1秦張儀帥師伐魏，取陝。

translations.literal: 1 Zhang Yi of Qin led troops against Wei and took Shan.
translations.idiomatic: 1 Zhang Yi of Qin invaded Wei and took Shan.

sentences.zh: 2蘇秦通-{於}-燕文公之夫人，易王知之。

translations.literal: 2 Su Qin had relations with the consort of Duke Wen of Yan; King Yi learned of it.
translations.idiomatic: 2 Su Qin lay with Duke Wen of Yan's queen; King Yi found out.

sentences.zh: 蘇秦恐，乃説易王曰：「臣居燕不能使燕重，而在齊則燕重。

translations.literal: Su Qin was afraid and therefore said to King Yi, “Your servant dwelling in Yan cannot make Yan weighty, but if I am in Qi then Yan grows weighty.
translations.idiomatic: Su Qin in fear told King Yi, “While I stay in Yan I cannot raise Yan's standing—but in Qi I can make Yan weighty.

sentences.zh: 」易王許之。

translations.literal: ” King Yi agreed.
translations.idiomatic: ” King Yi agreed.

sentences.zh: 乃偽得罪-{於}-燕而奔齊，齊宣王以爲客卿。

translations.literal: He then pretended to have offended Yan and fled to Qi; King Xuan of Qi made him guest minister.
translations.idiomatic: He feigned offense against Yan and fled to Qi; King Xuan of Qi made him a guest minister.

sentences.zh: 蘇秦説齊王髙宮室，大苑囿，以明得意，欲以敝齊而爲燕。

translations.literal: Su Qin urged the King of Qi to raise palaces high and enlarge parks and preserves, to display his triumph, intending to exhaust Qi for Yan's sake.
translations.idiomatic: Su Qin urged the King of Qi to build towering palaces and vast parks, flaunting his triumph, intending to wear Qi down for Yan.

sentences.zh: 1秦張儀及齊、楚之相會嚙桑。

translations.literal: 1 Zhang Yi of Qin and the chancellors of Qi and Chu met at Nie Sang.
translations.idiomatic: 1 Zhang Yi of Qin met the chancellors of Qi and Chu at Nie Sang.

sentences.zh: 2韓、燕皆稱王，趙武靈王獨不肯，曰：「無其實，敢處其名乎？

translations.literal: 2 Han and Yan both styled themselves kings; King Wuling of Zhao alone refused, saying, “Without the substance, how dare one hold the name?”
translations.idiomatic: 2 Han and Yan both took royal titles; King Wuling of Zhao alone refused: “Without the substance, who dares wear the name?”

translations.idiomatic: ” He ordered his people to call him lord.

sentences.zh: 1秦張儀自嚙桑還而免相，相魏。

translations.literal: 1 Zhang Yi of Qin, returning from Nie Sang, was removed as chancellor and became chancellor of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: 1 Zhang Yi returned from Nie Sang, left Qin's chancellorship, and became Wei's chancellor.

sentences.zh: 欲令魏先事秦而諸侯效之，魏王不-{聽}-。

translations.literal: He wished to make Wei serve Qin first so the feudal lords would follow; the King of Wei would not heed him.
translations.idiomatic: He meant Wei to serve Qin first so other lords would follow; the King of Wei refused.

sentences.zh: 秦王伐魏，取-{曲}-沃、平周。

translations.literal: The King of Qin attacked Wei and took Quwo and Pingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The King of Qin struck Wei and took Quwo and Pingzhou.

sentences.zh: -{復}-陰厚張儀益甚。

translations.literal: -{Again}-in secret he treated Zhang Yi all the more generously.
translations.idiomatic: In secret he treated Zhang Yi more generously than ever.

translations.idiomatic: 2 [Summer, fourth month]<ref>[Summer, fourth month]—from Shiji “Biography of Lord Mengchang,” Suoyin citing the Bamboo Annals.

translations.literal: </ref>, the King of Qi enfeoffed Tian Ying at Xue and styled him Lord Jingguo.
translations.idiomatic: </ref> the King of Qi enfeoffed Tian Ying at Xue as Lord Jingguo.

sentences.zh: 靖郭君言-{於}-齊王曰：「五官之計不可不日-{聽}-而數覽也」王從之，已而厭之，悉以委靖郭君。

translations.literal: Lord Jingguo said to the King of Qi, “The accounts of the five offices cannot go unreviewed day by day and perused often.” The king followed this counsel; later he grew weary of it and entrusted everything to Lord Jingguo.
translations.idiomatic: Lord Jingguo told the King of Qi, “The five bureaus' accounts must be heard daily and read often.” The king agreed; soon he tired of it and handed everything to Lord Jingguo.

sentences.zh: 由是得專政齊之權。

translations.literal: From this he came to monopolize government authority in Qi.
translations.idiomatic: From this he monopolized power in Qi.

sentences.zh: 靖郭君欲城薛，客謂靖郭君曰：「君不聞海大魚乎？

translations.literal: Lord Jing of Guo wished to fortify Xue; a guest said to him, “Have you not heard of the great fish of the sea?
translations.idiomatic: Lord Jing of Guo wished to wall Xue; a guest said to him, “Have you never heard of the great fish of the sea?

sentences.zh: 網不能止，鉤不能牽，蕩而失水，則螻蟻-{制}-焉。

translations.literal: Nets cannot hold it, hooks cannot draw it; cast adrift and losing the water, then ants and mole-crickets may master it.
translations.idiomatic: No net can hold it, no hook can haul it—adrift and stripped of water, ants and mole-crickets master it.

sentences.zh: 今夫齊，亦君之水也。

translations.literal: Now Qi, too, is your water.
translations.idiomatic: Qi is your water now.

sentences.zh: 君長有齊，奚以薛爲！

translations.literal: If you long hold Qi, what need have you of Xue!
translations.idiomatic: Hold Qi for life—what need of Xue!

sentences.zh: 苟爲失齊，雖隆薛之城到-{於}-天，庸足恃乎？

translations.literal: If you should lose Qi, though you piled Xue’s walls to heaven, how could you rely on them?
translations.idiomatic: Lose Qi, and though Xue’s walls reached the sky, what could you trust?

sentences.zh: 」乃不果城。

translations.literal: ” He then did not fortify it after all.
translations.idiomatic: ” He abandoned the fortification.

translations.idiomatic: Lord Jing of Guo had forty [-{餘}-] sons<ref>Lord Jing of Guo had forty [-{餘}-] sons—Zhang’s collation: the twelve-line edition has [-{餘}-] after “ten”;

translations.literal: the Yi eleven-line edition agrees;
translations.idiomatic: the Yi eleven-line edition agrees;

translations.literal: </ref>, and a son by a low concubine was called Wen.
translations.idiomatic: </ref>, and a son by a humble concubine was named Wen.

sentences.zh: 文通儻饒智略，説靖郭君以散財養士。

translations.literal: Wen was unrestrained and richly endowed with stratagems; he persuaded Lord Jing of Guo to scatter wealth and nourish retainers.
translations.idiomatic: Wen was bold and brimmed with stratagems; he urged Lord Jing of Guo to spend his fortune keeping men.

sentences.zh: 靖郭君使文主家待賓客，賓客爭譽其美，皆請靖郭君以文爲嗣。

translations.literal: Lord Jing of Guo had Wen manage the household and receive guests; guests vied to praise his excellence, and all asked Lord Jing of Guo to make Wen his heir.
translations.idiomatic: Lord Jing of Guo put Wen in charge of the house and guests; guests praised him to the skies, and all begged that Wen be made heir.

sentences.zh: 靖郭君卒，文嗣爲薛公，號曰孟嘗君。

translations.literal: When Lord Jing of Guo died, Wen succeeded as Lord of Xue and was styled Lord Mengchang.
translations.idiomatic: When Lord Jing of Guo died, Wen succeeded as Lord of Xue and took the title Lord Mengchang.

sentences.zh: 孟嘗君招致諸侯-{游}-士及有罪亡人，皆-{捨}-業厚遇之，存救其親戚。

translations.literal: Lord Mengchang gathered wandering scholars of the feudal lords and men guilty and in flight; all he treated with generous favor, abandoning their former trades, and he preserved and rescued their kin.
translations.idiomatic: Lord Mengchang gathered wandering scholars and fugitives from every state, lavished favors on them, and let them abandon their old callings while he saved their kin.

sentences.zh: 食客常數千人，各自以爲孟嘗君親己。

translations.literal: His retainers often numbered several thousand; each thought Lord Mengchang treated him as kin.
translations.idiomatic: His retainers often numbered in the thousands; each believed Lord Mengchang favored him alone.

sentences.zh: 由是孟嘗君之名重天下。

translations.literal: From this Lord Mengchang’s fame weighed heavy throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Lord Mengchang’s name weighed on the world.

sentences.zh: ::臣光曰：君子之養士，以爲民也。

translations.literal: :: Your servant Guang says: When a gentleman nourishes retainers, it is for the sake of the people.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Guang remarks: A gentleman keeps retainers for the people’s sake.

sentences.zh: 《易》曰：「聖人養賢，以及萬民。

translations.literal: The Changes says: “The sage nourishes the worthy to reach the myriad people.
translations.idiomatic: The Changes says: “The sage nourishes the worthy to reach the myriad people.

sentences.zh: 」夫賢者，其德足以敦化正俗，其-{才}-足以頓綱振紀，其明足以燭微慮遠，其強足以結仁固義。

translations.literal: ” The worthy man’s virtue suffices to deepen transformation and set customs right; his [-{才}-] suffices to brace the net and rouse the statutes; his clarity suffices to illumine the subtle and ponder the far; his strength suffices to bind benevolence and firm righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: ” The worthy man’s virtue can deepen custom and set the age right; his talent can brace the laws and rouse order; his clarity can pierce the subtle and see far; his strength can bind benevolence and firm loyalty.

sentences.zh: 大則利天下，小則利一國。

translations.literal: On a great scale he benefits all under heaven; on a small scale he benefits one state.
translations.idiomatic: At greatest he profits the realm; at least he profits one state.

sentences.zh: 是以君子-{豐}-祿以富之，隆爵以尊之。

translations.literal: Therefore the gentleman [-{豐}-] enriches him with ample stipend and honors him with exalted rank.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the gentleman heaps stipend and wealth on him and raises him in rank and honor.

sentences.zh: 養一人而及萬人者，養賢之道也。

translations.literal: To nourish one man and thereby reach ten thousand men—this is the Way of nourishing the worthy.
translations.idiomatic: To keep one man and thereby reach ten thousand—that is how the worthy are kept.

sentences.zh: 今孟嘗君之養士也，不恤智愚，不擇臧否，盜其君之祿，以立私黨，張虚譽，上以侮其君，下以蠹其民，是-{奸}-人之雄也，烏足尚哉！

translations.literal: Now in Lord Mengchang’s nourishing of retainers he does not care whether they are wise or foolish, does not choose good or bad; he steals his lord’s stipends to build a private faction, spreads empty fame, above insults his ruler, below harms the people—he is chief among [-{奸}-] men; how is he fit to be esteemed!
translations.idiomatic: Lord Mengchang keeps men without regard to wit or folly, good or ill; he steals his ruler’s pay to build a private faction, trades in hollow fame, insults his prince above and devours the people below—chief among villains; what is there to admire!

sentences.zh: 《書》曰：「受爲天下逋逃主、萃淵藪。

translations.literal: The Documents says: “Zhou was lord of fugitives for all under heaven, a gathering pool and deep lair.
translations.idiomatic: The Documents says: “Zhou was lord of fugitives for all under heaven, a gathering pool and deep lair.

sentences.zh: 」此之謂也。

translations.literal: ” This is what is meant.
translations.idiomatic: ” This is what is meant.

sentences.zh: 1王崩，子愼靚王定立。

translations.literal: 1 The king died; his son King Shenjing, Ding, was established.
translations.idiomatic: 1 The Zhou king died; his son King Shenjing Ding succeeded.

sentences.zh: 2燕易王薨，子噲立。

translations.literal: 2 King Yi of Yan died; his son Kuai succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: 2 King Yi of Yan died; his son Kuai succeeded.

sentences.zh: 3孟嘗君聘-{於}-楚，楚王遺之象床。

translations.literal: 3 Lord Mengchang went on a mission to Chu; the king of Chu sent him off with a couch of ivory.
translations.idiomatic: 3 Lord Mengchang went on a mission to Chu; the king of Chu gave him an ivory couch as a parting gift.

sentences.zh: 登徒直送之，不欲行，謂孟嘗君門人公孫戌曰：「象床之直千金，苟傷之毫-{髮}-，則賣妻子不足償也。

translations.literal: Dengtu Zhi was to escort it but did not wish to go; he said to Gongsun Xu, a retainer of Lord Mengchang, “The ivory couch is worth a thousand in gold; if a single [-{髮}-] of it is harmed, selling wife and children would not suffice to pay.
translations.idiomatic: Dengtu Zhi was to escort it but refused; he told Gongsun Xu, a retainer of Lord Mengchang, “The ivory couch is worth a thousand in gold; scratch a single hair of it and selling wife and children would not cover the debt.

sentences.zh: 足下能使-{僕}-無行者，有先人之寶劍，-{願}-獻之。

translations.literal: If you, sir, can make [-{僕}-] not go, I have my forefathers’ treasured sword and [-{願}-] offer it.
translations.idiomatic: If you can spare me the journey, I have my forefathers’ treasured sword and would give it to you.

sentences.zh: 」公孫戌許諾，入見孟嘗君曰：「小國所以皆致相印-{於}-君者，以君能振達貧窮，存亡繼絶，故莫不悅君之義，慕君之廉也。

translations.literal: ” Gongsun Xu promised, entered, and saw Lord Mengchang, saying, “The reason small states all bestow their seals of chancellor on you is that you can raise up the poor, preserve states on the verge of ruin and continue severed lineages; therefore none fail to delight in your righteousness and admire your integrity.
translations.idiomatic: ” Gongsun Xu agreed, went in, and told Lord Mengchang, “Small states lend you their chancellor’s seal because you lift the poor, save dying kingdoms, and continue broken lines—everyone delights in your righteousness and admires your integrity.

sentences.zh: 今始至楚而受象床，則未至之國將何以待君哉！

translations.literal: Now, having just reached Chu, you accept an ivory couch—how will states you have not yet reached receive you!
translations.idiomatic: Accept an ivory couch the moment you reach Chu, and what will the states you have not yet visited think of you!

sentences.zh: 」孟嘗君曰：「善。

translations.literal: ” Lord Mengchang said, “Well said.
translations.idiomatic: ” Lord Mengchang said, “Good.

sentences.zh: 」遂不受。

translations.literal: ” He then did not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: ” He refused the gift.

sentences.zh: 公孫戌趨去，未至中閨，孟嘗君召而反之，曰：「子何足之髙，-{志}-之揚也？

translations.literal: Gongsun Xu hurried away; before reaching the inner court Lord Mengchang summoned him back and said, “Why are your feet so high, your [-{志}-] so lifted?
translations.idiomatic: Gongsun Xu hurried off; before he reached the inner court Lord Mengchang called him back: “Why the high step, the lifted brow?

sentences.zh: 」公孫戌以實對。

translations.literal: ” Gongsun Xu answered with the truth.
translations.idiomatic: ” Gongsun Xu told him the whole truth.

sentences.zh: 孟嘗君乃書門版曰：「有能揚文之名，止文之過，私得寶-{於}-外者，疾入諫！

translations.literal: Lord Mengchang then wrote on the gate board: “Whoever can spread Wen’s fame, stop Wen’s faults, or has privately received treasure from without—hurry in with remonstrance!
translations.idiomatic: Lord Mengchang then posted on the gate: “Whoever can spread Wen’s good name, check Wen’s faults, or has taken private gifts from abroad—come in at once and speak!

sentences.zh: ::臣光曰：孟嘗君可謂能用諫矣。

translations.literal: :: Your servant Guang says: Lord Mengchang may be called one who could use remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Guang remarks: Lord Mengchang may be said to have known how to heed counsel.

sentences.zh: 苟其言之善也，雖懷詐諼之心，猶將用之，況盡忠無私以事其上乎！

translations.literal: If the words are good, though one harbors a heart of deceitful flattery, he would still employ them—how much more one who serves his superior with full loyalty and no selfishness!
translations.idiomatic: If the words are sound, he would use them even from a flatterer with a deceitful heart—how much more from a man who serves his lord with full loyalty and no private aim!

sentences.zh: 《詩》-{云}-：「采葑采菲，無以下體。

translations.literal: The Odes [-{云}-]: “Gather turnip tops, gather radish leaves; do not reject them for the lower part.
translations.idiomatic: The Odes say: “Gather turnip tops, gather radish leaves; do not reject them for the lower part.

sentences.zh: 」孟嘗君有焉。

translations.literal: ” Lord Mengchang had this.
translations.idiomatic: ” Lord Mengchang had this.

sentences.zh: 4韓宣惠王欲兩用公仲、公叔爲政，問-{於}-繆留。

translations.literal: 4 King Xuanhui of Han wished to employ both Gongsun Zhong and Gongsun Shu in government and questioned Miu Liu.
translations.idiomatic: 4 King Xuanhui of Han wished to use both Gongsun Zhong and Gongsun Shu in power and asked Miu Liu.

sentences.zh: 對曰：「不可。

translations.literal: He replied, “It cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: He replied, “No.

sentences.zh: 晉用六卿而國分，齊簡公用陳成子及闞止而見殺，魏用犀首、張儀而西河之外亡。

translations.literal: Jin employed the Six Clans and the state was divided; Duke Jian of Qi employed Chen Chengzi and Kan Zhi and was killed; Wei employed Xishou and Zhang Yi and lost the lands beyond the Western River.
translations.idiomatic: Jin used the Six Clans and the state split; Duke Jian of Qi used Chen Chengzi and Kan Zhi and was murdered; Wei used Gongsun Yan and Zhang Yi and lost everything west of the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 今君兩用之，其多力者内樹黨，其寡力者藉外權。

translations.literal: Now if you employ both, the stronger will build factions within, the weaker will borrow power from without.
translations.idiomatic: Use both now and the stronger will build factions at home while the weaker leans on foreign power.

sentences.zh: 群臣有内樹黨以驕主，有外爲交以削地，君之國危矣！

translations.literal: When ministers build factions within to make the lord arrogant, or make alliances without to carve away territory, your state is in peril!
translations.idiomatic: When ministers build factions at home to browbeat their lord and make alliances abroad to carve away land, your state is in peril!
